summary: Late pin consensus on orchestrator causes dual routing to canary and stable variants for tenant streams
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary rollout for redwood/open-7b-v2 in us-east, a subset of tenant streaming sessions (Luminary Health) observed mixed responses coming from both canary and stable model variants within the same session. Impact: Customer reports hallucinated output variance and occasional schema mismatch when the stream switched mid-session. Approx 12% of active streams for the tenant were affected over a 22-minute window.

Environment: production us-east cluster; Dedicated capacity pool for Luminary Health; orchestrator service version v2.14.0-hotfix applied 2026-03-11T11:20Z.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Start long-running streaming session via tenant API key in us-east targeting route "/v1/chat/streams". 2) Trigger multiple rapid prefix messages to force KV-cache warmups and routing evaluation. 3) Observe session-level variant header and returned model id across token batches.

Observed behavior: Sessions that began pinned to stable variant occasionally received token batches from canary until session ended. Edge logs show duplicated commit attempts to the pin registry with different commit timestamps. Orchestrator logs show delayed quorum acknowledgement for pin commit on ~50 shards.

Expected behavior: Once a session is pinned to a model variant, all requests in that session should be routed consistently to that variant until explicit unpin or session termination.

Temporary workaround: Rolled back orchestrator hotfix to previous stable binary at 2026-03-11T12:05Z which reduced dual-routing to <0.5% for the affected tenant. Advised Luminary to restart any long-running streams as a mitigation for in-flight mixed responses.
investigation_notes: 11:25 UTC - Customer CS reports mixed-model outputs; initial triage by support suggests pin inconsistency.
11:32 UTC - Checked edge-proxy metrics: increased pin commit latency spike starting at 11:20 UTC coincident with orchestrator hotpatch rollout.
11:45 UTC - Orchestrator leader reported short leader election and multiple in-flight commit retries to pin-registry (etcd) - observed 200-400ms extra latency per commit on 50/512 shards.
11:52 UTC - Correlated with a recent change in orchestrator which optimistically updated in-memory routing before commit ack from pin-registry to reduce tail latency (PR referenced below).

12:00 UTC - Reproduced locally with synthetic load: when commit ack delayed beyond threshold, edge cache entries were refreshed from memory and could carry stale shard maps, resulting in mixed routing for multiplexed session streams.
12:10 UTC - Rollback of orchestrator hotfix performed; monitoring showed pin commit latency returned to baseline and mixed routing rates dropped sharply.

Hypothesis: A race introduced by optimistic in-memory route promotion combined with transient etcd latency caused a window where edge nodes accepted an unconfirmed pin state and routed some requests to the canary while other nodes retained the stable mapping, producing interleaved responses for the same session.
Related logs: edge-proxy trace ids 7f2a9b..7f2aef with duplicated commit signatures; orchestrator log excerpt: "WARN commit: shard=153 ack_wait=412ms optimistic_promote=true".

root_cause: Race between optimistic in-memory route promotion and delayed commit acknowledgement from the pin-registry (etcd). The orchestrator's hotfix allowed routes to be visible to some edge nodes before a durable commit completed, causing inconsistent routing decisions across the cluster during transient leader/latency events.
resolution: Rolled back v2.14.0-hotfix to v2.13.9 across us-east dedicated pool. Implemented temporary guard in orchestrator to require commit ack before promoting route to edge cache. Disabled optimistic promotion flag for subsequent canary runs. Created follow-up engineering task to add commit ack telemetry and stricter TTL refresh coordination (see linked PRs).
resolution_notes: Temporary guard added to orchestrator at 2026-03-11T13:00Z and deployed via hotpatch across us-east.
Edge-side validation added to reject route changes without commit signature by 2026-03-12.
Customer Luminary Health verified significant reduction in mixed responses; asked for postmortem and runbook entry.
Follow-up: ENG-2345 to implement commit-ack gating and ENG-2346 to add pin commit SLO alerts.
next_steps: Complete ENG-2345 and ENG-2346 (owner: Marco Ruiz) before next canary rollout to any dedicated pools.
Add a canary gating check to block optimistic promotion when multiple shards report ack latency >100ms.
Add tenant-level notification to affected customers when pin state transitions are observed during rollout window.
Run controlled chaos test on pin-registry latency to validate guard logic.
Publish incident report and notify Luminary Health (CS owner: Aisha Patel).
